name: Tiong Bahru
summary: Art-deco grids, café culture, wet-market groceries, and central living with more texture than Orchard towers.
body: Tiong Bahru’s low-rise heritage estate and surrounding condos attract people who want central access without Marina Bay gloss. Independent cafés, the wet market (produce and seafood for home cooks), and park connectors set the rhythm — a practical grocery alternative to FairPrice-only or RedMart-default living. Week-one expats who learn the market’s morning fish and late-day clearance prices often cut delivery fees and platform charges that online grocery threads complain about. Units can be compact; demand keeps rents firm. Older walk-ups still need aircon servicing discipline and chute/pest awareness; ceiling-slab leak fights follow HDB owner rules if you rent a flat rather than a boutique condo. It works well for couples and small families who prioritise walkability and character over school-corridor adjacency. Weekend tourist footfall is real; weekday mornings at the market are calmer. Pet households: confirm landlord + estate rules in writing — heritage blocks and nearby towers are not one policy.
housingMix: Heritage walk-ups, boutique apartments, nearby towers.
commuteNotes: East-West Line at Tiong Bahru; short hop to Outram and Chinatown.
